course.title: Cocktail and Mocktail Making
course.tagline: Mix classic and signature drinks, with and without alcohol, for any event.

days.title: Cocktail Basics: Tools and Words
days.goal: Know your bar tools and the basic words.
steps: Find your tools: a shaker, a jigger (a small measurer), a spoon, and a strainer.
A jigger measures drink amounts. One side is bigger, one is smaller.
A shaker is a metal cup you shake drinks in with ice.
A strainer is a sieve that holds back the ice when you pour.
Learn the words: shake, stir, muddle (press), strain, and garnish (decorate).
days.task: List your bar tools and measure water with a jigger.
days.challenge: Practise shaking water and ice in a shaker.

options: A small measurer for drink amounts
quiz.explain: A jigger measures the exact amount of each drink ingredient.

options: Shaking drinks with ice to mix and chill them
quiz.explain: A shaker mixes and chills a drink fast with ice.

options: To press fruit or herbs gently to release flavour
quiz.explain: Muddling presses fruit or herbs gently to release their flavour.

days.title: How to Shake a Cocktail
days.goal: Shake a cocktail the right way.
steps: Fill the shaker with ice first.
Add your ingredients. Measure each one with a jigger.
Close the shaker tight. Hold both ends.
Shake hard for 10 to 15 seconds. The shaker will feel cold.
Open it and strain the drink into a glass.
days.task: Shake a simple drink with water, juice, and ice.
days.challenge: Shake the same drink twice and compare how cold it gets.

quiz.q: Why fill the shaker with ice first?
options: Ice chills and mixes the drink as you shake
quiz.explain: Ice chills the drink and helps mix it while you shake.
Ten to fifteen seconds is enough to chill and mix a drink.

quiz.q: How do you know a shake is done?
options: The shaker feels cold on the outside
quiz.explain: A cold shaker means the drink inside is cold.

days.title: How to Stir a Cocktail
days.goal: Stir a cocktail smoothly with a long spoon.
steps: Some drinks are stirred, not shaken. Clear drinks are usually stirred.
Fill a mixing glass with ice.
Add your ingredients and stir with a long spoon for 30 seconds.
Stir in circles. Do not splash.
Strain into a cold glass.
days.task: Stir a simple drink with juice and water.
days.challenge: Stir one drink and shake the same drink, then compare.

quiz.explain: Clear drinks are stirred so they stay clear and smooth.
About 30 seconds chills and mixes the drink.

quiz.q: Why stir in circles without splashing?
options: Smooth stirring keeps the drink clear
quiz.explain: Gentle, circular stirring keeps the drink smooth and clear.

days.title: How to Muddle: Mint and Fruit
days.goal: Muddle mint and fruit gently.

video.title: How to Shake a Cocktail Like a Pro

steps: Muddling means pressing gently with a muddler or a spoon.
Put mint leaves in the glass with sugar and lime.
Press gently 3 or 4 times. Do not tear the leaves.
Torn mint tastes bitter. Gentle pressing releases the oils.
Add ice and the rest of the drink, then stir.
days.task: Muddle mint with sugar and lime in a glass.
days.challenge: Muddle too hard on purpose once and taste the difference.

options: Presses gently to release flavour from herbs or fruit
quiz.explain: Muddling presses herbs or fruit gently to release their flavour.
Torn mint releases bitter tastes. Gentle pressing is best.

quiz.q: How many times should you press?
quiz.explain: Three or four gentle presses are enough.

days.title: The Mojito: Your First Classic
days.goal: Make a mojito, step by step.
steps: A mojito is rum, mint, lime, sugar, and soda water.
Put mint, sugar, and lime wedges in a tall glass. Muddle gently.
Fill the glass with ice.
Add rum. Top up with soda water.
Stir gently and add a mint leaf on top.
days.task: Make a mojito.
days.challenge: Make a mocktail mojito with no rum and compare.

options: Rum, mint, lime, sugar, and soda water
quiz.explain: A mojito is rum, mint, lime, sugar, and soda water.

quiz.q: What glass does a mojito go in?
quiz.explain: A mojito is served in a tall glass with lots of ice.
A mocktail has no alcohol. It uses soda and juice instead.

days.title: Straining and Layering
days.goal: Strain a drink cleanly and layer a drink.

video.title: The Basic Cocktail Techniques 101: Shake, Stir, and Sip Like a Pro

steps: Straining means pouring through a strainer to hold back ice.
Hold the strainer over the shaker and pour slowly.
Layering means pouring drinks on top of each other so they stay separate.
Pour the heaviest drink first, then the lighter one over the back of a spoon.
Pour slowly. Fast pouring mixes the layers.
days.task: Strain a shaken drink into a glass.
days.challenge: Layer two juices in a glass using a spoon.

options: Holds back ice when you pour
quiz.explain: A strainer holds the ice back so only the drink pours out.

options: Pouring drinks so they stay in separate layers
quiz.explain: Layering stacks drinks in separate bands of colour.

quiz.q: Why pour over the back of a spoon?
options: It slows the pour so layers stay separate
quiz.explain: A slow pour over a spoon stops the drinks mixing.

days.title: Week 1 Project: A Drinks Tasting
days.goal: Make three drinks and taste them side by side.
steps: Make a mojito, a stirred drink, and a layered drink.
Serve them in the right glasses with ice.
Write a tasting note for each: sweet, sour, strong, or fresh.
Ask tasters which one they like best and why.
Pick your favourite and write the recipe down.
days.task: Make three drinks and hold a tasting for your household.
days.challenge: Write tasting notes for each drink.

quiz.q: Why taste three drinks side by side?
quiz.explain: Tasting side by side makes the differences in taste clear.

options: A short note on how a drink tastes
quiz.explain: A tasting note is a short description of the flavour.

quiz.q: Why write the recipe for your favourite?
options: So you can make it the same way every time
quiz.explain: A written recipe lets you repeat a good drink.

project.title: Hold a Drinks Tasting
project.brief: Make a mojito, a stirred drink, and a layered drink, and taste them.
checks: Each drink served in the right glass
Tasting notes written for all three

days.title: Easy Cocktails for Beginners
days.goal: Make five easy cocktails with few ingredients.
steps: Easy cocktails use only 2 or 3 ingredients.
Screwdriver: vodka and orange juice.
Gin and tonic: gin and tonic water with lime.
Rum and coke: rum and cola with lime.
Make each one in a glass with ice. Stir gently.
days.task: Make three easy cocktails.
days.challenge: Make a second round and try different amounts.

options: Only 2 or 3 ingredients and no hard steps
quiz.explain: Easy cocktails use few ingredients and simple steps.
A screwdriver is vodka and orange juice.

quiz.q: What is in a gin and tonic?
options: Gin and tonic water with lime
quiz.explain: A gin and tonic is gin, tonic water, and lime.

days.title: The B52: A Layered Shot
days.goal: Make a B52, a layered shot drink.
steps: A B52 has three layers: coffee liqueur, cream liqueur, and orange liqueur.
Pour the coffee liqueur first. It is the heaviest.
Pour the cream liqueur slowly over the back of a spoon.
Pour the orange liqueur the same way on top.
Serve at once. Do not stir it.
days.task: Make a B52.
days.challenge: Practise layering with juice and water first if you want to save money.

options: Coffee liqueur, cream liqueur, and orange liqueur
quiz.explain: A B52 is three liqueurs layered in a shot glass.

quiz.q: Why pour the heaviest drink first?
options: Heavy drinks sink, so they form the bottom layer
quiz.explain: The heaviest drink sinks to the bottom and the lighter ones float on top.

options: Stirring mixes the layers and ruins the look
quiz.explain: A B52 is all about the layers. Stirring destroys them.

days.title: Bloody Mary: The Savoury Classic
days.goal: Make a Bloody Mary.
steps: A Bloody Mary is vodka, tomato juice, and spices.
Add lemon juice, salt, pepper, and a drop of hot sauce.
Shake or roll the drink between two tins to mix it.
Pour over ice in a tall glass.
Add a celery stick or a lemon wedge on top.
days.task: Make a Bloody Mary.
days.challenge: Make a virgin Bloody Mary with no vodka and compare.

quiz.q: What is in a Bloody Mary?
quiz.explain: A Bloody Mary is vodka, tomato juice, lemon, and spices.

quiz.q: What makes a Bloody Mary spicy?
quiz.explain: Hot sauce and pepper give a Bloody Mary its kick.

quiz.q: What is a virgin Bloody Mary?
options: A Bloody Mary with more vodka
A Bloody Mary with no alcohol
A Bloody Mary with no tomato
quiz.explain: Virgin means no alcohol. It uses tomato juice and spices only.

days.title: Vodka Cocktails: Five Easy Ones
days.goal: Make five easy vodka cocktails.

video.title: Mixology Techniques: Mastering Shaking, Stirring, and Muddling

steps: Blue Lagoon: vodka, blue curacao, lime, and soda.
Screwdriver: vodka and orange juice.
Vodka Sunrise: vodka, orange juice, and grenadine.
Madras: vodka, cranberry juice, and orange juice.
Make each one in a glass with ice and a lemon slice.
days.task: Make three vodka cocktails.
days.challenge: Make the other two the next day and pick a favourite.

quiz.q: What is in a Blue Lagoon?
options: Vodka, blue curacao, lime, and soda
quiz.explain: A Blue Lagoon is vodka, blue curacao, lime mix, and soda.

quiz.q: What gives a Vodka Sunrise its colour?
quiz.explain: Grenadine sinks and makes the sunrise look at the bottom.

options: Vodka, cranberry juice, and orange juice
quiz.explain: A Madras is vodka with cranberry and orange juice.

days.title: Mocktails: Drinks Without Alcohol
days.goal: Make five mocktails for everyone.

video.title: Easy Cocktails for Beginners: Simple Recipes to Get You Started

steps: A mocktail is a cocktail with no alcohol.
Use juice, soda, and fresh fruit instead of alcohol.
Spiced Lime Refresher: lime, soda, and a little spice.
Fruit mocktail: orange juice, cranberry juice, and soda.
Serve in the same nice glasses as cocktails.
days.task: Make three mocktails.
days.challenge: Serve a mocktail to someone who does not drink alcohol.

quiz.explain: A mocktail has no alcohol. It uses juice, soda, and fruit.

quiz.q: What do you use instead of alcohol?
quiz.explain: Juice, soda, and fresh fruit replace alcohol in a mocktail.

quiz.q: Why serve mocktails in nice glasses?
options: So everyone feels included at a party
quiz.explain: Nice glasses make mocktails feel special, not second best.

days.title: Garnishes: The Finishing Touch
days.goal: Garnish drinks so they look professional.
steps: A garnish is a decoration on a drink.
Use a lemon or lime wedge, a mint leaf, or a fruit slice.
Cut a lemon twist: a thin strip of peel twisted over the drink.
Put the garnish on the edge of the glass or floating on top.
Keep it simple. One garnish is enough.
days.task: Garnish three drinks with different garnishes.
days.challenge: Make a lemon twist and use it on a drink.

quiz.explain: A garnish is a decoration, like a lemon wedge or a mint leaf.

options: A thin strip of lemon peel twisted over a drink
quiz.explain: A lemon twist is a thin strip of peel that adds scent and looks smart.

quiz.q: How many garnishes should a drink have?
quiz.explain: One neat garnish looks professional. Too many look messy.

days.title: Week 2 Project: A Cocktail Menu
days.goal: Make a cocktail menu with five drinks.

video.title: A Refreshing Mocktail With Almost No Calories!

steps: Pick five drinks: a mojito, an easy cocktail, a layered drink, a mocktail, and a vodka cocktail.
Write the recipes with exact amounts.
Make all five and serve them in the right glasses.
Garnish each one neatly.
Ask tasters to pick a favourite and set a price for each drink.
days.task: Make a five-drink cocktail menu.
days.challenge: Price each drink as if you were selling it.

options: A menu with five choices shows your range
quiz.explain: Five drinks show you can run a real drinks menu.

options: A garnish makes the drink look professional
quiz.explain: A neat garnish shows care and makes the drink look worth buying.

options: So you know what to charge and what you earn
quiz.explain: Pricing tells you the profit on each drink.

project.title: Make a Five-Drink Cocktail Menu
project.brief: Make five drinks, garnished and served in the right glasses.
checks: Each drink in the right glass

days.title: Glassware: The Right Glass
days.goal: Learn which glass goes with which drink.
steps: A tall glass is for long drinks like a mojito.
A short glass is for strong drinks on ice.
A wine glass is for drinks served without ice.
A shot glass is for small layered drinks.
Chill glasses in the fridge before serving.
days.task: Serve three drinks in the right glasses.
days.challenge: Chill glasses in the fridge and note the difference.

quiz.q: What glass is a mojito served in?
quiz.explain: A mojito is a long drink, so it goes in a tall glass.

quiz.q: What glass is a B52 served in?
quiz.explain: A B52 is a small layered drink, so it goes in a shot glass.

options: A cold glass keeps the drink cold longer
quiz.explain: A chilled glass keeps the drink cold and fresh.

days.title: Ice: The Secret Ingredient
days.goal: Use ice well in cocktails.
steps: Ice chills a drink and adds a little water as it melts.
Use fresh, clear ice. Old ice from the freezer can taste bad.
Big ice cubes melt slower than small ones.
Crushed ice is best for drinks like a mojito.
Fill the glass with ice before you pour.
days.task: Make drinks with big ice cubes and with crushed ice.
days.challenge: Compare how fast each one melts.

quiz.q: What does ice do in a drink?
options: Chills the drink and adds a little water
quiz.explain: Ice chills the drink and adds a little water as it melts.

options: They melt slower, so the drink stays strong
quiz.explain: Big cubes melt slowly, so the drink does not get watery fast.

quiz.q: Why fill the glass with ice before pouring?
options: So the drink chills at once
quiz.explain: A full glass of ice chills the drink the moment you pour.

days.title: Simple Syrup: The Sweetener
days.goal: Make simple syrup for cocktails.
steps: Simple syrup is sugar dissolved in water.
Mix equal parts sugar and water in a pot.
Heat gently and stir until the sugar disappears.
Cool it and store it in a sealed bottle in the fridge.
Use a small amount in drinks. It mixes better than dry sugar.
days.task: Make a bottle of simple syrup.
days.challenge: Use it in a drink and compare with dry sugar.

quiz.explain: Simple syrup is equal parts sugar and water, heated until the sugar melts.

quiz.q: Why use syrup instead of dry sugar?
options: Syrup mixes into cold drinks. Dry sugar does not
quiz.explain: Dry sugar does not melt in cold drinks. Syrup mixes in easily.

quiz.q: How long does simple syrup keep?
quiz.explain: In a sealed bottle in the fridge, it keeps about 2 weeks.

days.title: Signature Drinks: Make Your Own
days.goal: Create your own signature cocktail and mocktail.

video.title: How to Shake a Cocktail Like a Pro

steps: Pick a base: a spirit for a cocktail, juice for a mocktail.
Add a fruit flavour you love.
Add something sour like lime, and something sweet like syrup.
Taste it and adjust. Write the recipe down.
Give it a name.
days.task: Create your own cocktail and mocktail.
days.challenge: Serve them to a friend and ask what they think.

options: A drink with a fancy name
quiz.explain: A signature drink is one you created and can make well.

quiz.q: What three tastes should a drink balance?
options: Sweet, sour, and the base flavour
quiz.explain: A good drink balances sweet, sour, and its main flavour.

options: A name makes it easy to sell and remember
quiz.explain: A named drink is a product you can sell.

days.title: Costing Drinks: Price Your Menu
days.goal: Work out what each drink costs and what to charge.
steps: List every ingredient with its price.
Add the cost of the glass, garnish, and ice.
Divide the total by the number of drinks you made.
Charge 3 to 4 times the cost for a profit.
Compare with bars near you.
days.task: Cost a mojito and set its selling price.
days.challenge: Cost a mocktail the same way.

quiz.q: What is the cost per drink?
options: Total cost divided by the number of drinks
quiz.explain: Cost per drink is the total cost shared across all the drinks you made.

quiz.q: Why charge 3 to 4 times the cost?
options: To cover rent, power, and your time, and still make a profit
quiz.explain: Bars have rent and power costs, so drinks are priced higher than home costs.

quiz.q: What else must you add to the cost?
quiz.explain: Glasses, garnishes, and ice are real costs of every drink.

days.title: Drink Mistakes and Fixes
days.goal: Fix the commonest cocktail problems.

video.title: The Basic Cocktail Techniques 101: Shake, Stir, and Sip Like a Pro

steps: Drink is too strong? Add more mixer, like soda or juice.
Drink is too sweet? Add more lime juice.
Drink is too sour? Add a little simple syrup.
Drink is cloudy when it should be clear? You shook it. Stir it next time.
Write down each problem and fix.
days.task: Fix one drink problem you have had.
days.challenge: Make a drink, taste it, and adjust it three ways.

quiz.q: What do you do if a drink is too strong?
options: Add more mixer like soda or juice
quiz.explain: More mixer softens a strong drink.

quiz.q: What do you do if a drink is too sweet?
quiz.explain: Lime juice balances sweetness.

quiz.q: Why is a stirred drink cloudy?
options: You shook it instead of stirring
quiz.explain: Shaking adds tiny air bubbles that make a drink cloudy.

days.title: Week 3 Project: A Drinks Night
days.goal: Run a drinks night for friends or family.
steps: Pick the menu: three cocktails and two mocktails.
Write the recipes, costs, and prices.
Set up your bar station the night before.
Make each drink to order and serve it in the right glass.
Ask guests to vote for their favourite.
days.task: Run a drinks night for at least 4 people.
days.challenge: Cost the night and work out your profit if you sold the drinks.

quiz.q: Why set up the night before?
quiz.explain: Setting up early means no rushing when guests arrive.
Drinks made to order are cold and fresh.

options: So everyone has something to drink
quiz.explain: Mocktails mean guests who do not drink alcohol still enjoy the night.

project.title: Run a Drinks Night
project.brief: Serve three cocktails and two mocktails to at least 4 people.
checks: Five different drinks made to order
Each drink in the right glass

days.title: Responsible Serving
days.goal: Serve alcohol safely and responsibly.
steps: Never serve alcohol to anyone under the legal drinking age.
Do not serve someone who has had too much to drink.
Always offer water and food with alcohol.
Always offer mocktails and soft drinks too.
Know the law in your area and follow it.
days.task: Write a short list of responsible serving rules for your bar.
days.challenge: Practise offering water and food with a drink.

quiz.q: Who should you never serve alcohol to?
options: Children and anyone under the legal age
quiz.explain: Never serve alcohol to anyone under the legal drinking age.

options: Water helps guests stay safe and hydrated
quiz.explain: Water helps guests drink safely.

options: So everyone has a good drink, even if they do not drink alcohol
quiz.explain: Mocktails include everyone at the party.

days.title: Bar Setup: Your Home Bar
days.goal: Set up a small home bar.
steps: Pick a clean, flat surface for your bar.
Keep your tools, glasses, and ingredients in one place.
Keep ice in a cooler or a bowl with a lid.
Keep a cloth nearby for spills.
Write a small menu and put it where guests can see it.
days.task: Set up your home bar station.
days.challenge: Make a drink at your bar and time how long it takes.

quiz.q: What do you need for a home bar?
options: Tools, glasses, ingredients, and ice in one place
quiz.explain: A home bar needs your tools, glasses, ingredients, and ice together.
Spills happen. A cloth nearby keeps the bar clean.

options: So guests know what they can order
quiz.explain: A menu tells guests what drinks you can make.

days.title: Your Signature Cocktail
days.goal: Choose and perfect one cocktail you can make brilliantly.
steps: Pick the cocktail your household loves most from this course.
Write the recipe in your own words with exact amounts.
Make it again, timing every step and noting problems.
Fix the problems and make it once more.
Get someone new to taste it and give honest feedback.
days.task: Make your signature cocktail and write the final recipe down.
days.challenge: Make it for someone new and record what they say.

options: A cocktail you can make brilliantly every time
A cocktail with a fancy name
quiz.explain: A signature cocktail is one you have mastered.

quiz.q: Why write the recipe in your own words?
options: So you truly understand it and can repeat it
quiz.explain: Writing it yourself proves you understand each step.

quiz.q: Why get a new person to taste it?
quiz.explain: People who know you may be polite. New tasters are honest.

days.title: Drinks Business: First Steps
days.goal: Take your first steps toward selling drinks.

video.title: Mixology Techniques: Mastering Shaking, Stirring, and Muddling

steps: Pick 3 or 4 drinks to sell. Keep the menu small.
Set your prices from your costing work.
Take clear photos of your drinks in good light.
Tell friends and family first. Ask them to share.
Take orders in advance so you buy only what you need.
days.task: Take photos of your best drinks and show them to three people.
days.challenge: Take one real order, even a small one, and serve it on time.

quiz.q: Why start with only 3 or 4 drinks?
options: A small menu is easier to make well and cost
quiz.explain: A small menu keeps quality high and costing simple.

options: So you buy only what you need and waste nothing
quiz.explain: Advance orders mean no waste and no guessing.

options: Clear photos help people decide to buy
quiz.explain: People buy with their eyes first. Good photos sell drinks.

days.title: Keeping Records: Orders and Money
days.goal: Keep simple records of your drinks business.

video.title: Easy Cocktails for Beginners: Simple Recipes to Get You Started

steps: Write down every order: what, how many, who, and when.
Write down what you spent and what you earned.
Work out your profit each week.
Note which drinks sell best and which do not.
Keep your money for drinks separate from your spending money.
days.task: Start a simple order book today, on paper or on your phone.
days.challenge: Work out your profit from one drinks night.

options: So nothing is forgotten and you know what to make
quiz.explain: Written orders stop mistakes and show what sells.

options: What is left after costs are taken from what you earned
quiz.explain: Profit is what remains after you pay for ingredients, glasses, and ice.

options: So you always know if the business is making money
quiz.explain: Separate money shows the true profit of your business.

days.title: Event Drinks: Weddings and Parties
days.goal: Plan drinks for a wedding or party.
steps: Ask how many guests and how long the party lasts.
Plan 2 drinks per guest for the first hour, then 1 per hour.
Make a big batch of one signature drink in advance.
Keep mocktails ready for guests who do not drink alcohol.
Keep ice cold and glasses clean all night.
days.task: Plan drinks for a party of 20 on paper.
days.challenge: Make a big batch of a mocktail for a group.

quiz.q: How many drinks should you plan per guest?
options: 2 in the first hour, then 1 per hour
quiz.explain: Two drinks in the first hour, then one per hour, is a good guide.

quiz.q: Why make a big batch in advance?
options: It saves time during the party
quiz.explain: A big batch made early means you serve fast all night.

options: So non-drinkers always have a good drink
quiz.explain: Mocktails include everyone at the party.

days.title: Drink Trends: What Customers Want
days.goal: Try new drink ideas and see what customers like.

video.title: A Refreshing Mocktail With Almost No Calories!

steps: Try a new fruit combination each week.
Ask customers what flavours they want.
Try a new garnish or a new glass.
Watch what other bars serve and learn from them.
Keep what works. Drop what does not sell.
days.task: Try a new drink combination today.
days.challenge: Ask three people what drink flavour they would like to try.

options: New flavours keep customers coming back
quiz.explain: New flavours give customers a reason to return.

quiz.q: Why ask customers what they want?
options: Customers buy what they asked for
quiz.explain: Asking customers tells you what will sell.

quiz.q: Why drop drinks that do not sell?
options: So you do not waste money on ingredients nobody wants
quiz.explain: A drink that does not sell wastes ingredients and money.

days.title: Revision: The Bartender's Skills Check
days.goal: Revisit the core skills of the course.
steps: Shake a cocktail from memory, without help.
Stir a drink and explain when to stir, not shake.
Muddle mint gently and explain why.
Name the tools: shaker, jigger, strainer, and muddler.
List your three strongest drinks and one to improve.
days.task: Make a full drinks menu from memory, no recipe.
days.challenge: Teach one drink skill from this course to a friend or family member.

quiz.q: When do you stir, not shake?
options: For clear drinks, so they stay clear
quiz.explain: Clear drinks are stirred so they stay smooth and clear.

options: It proves you really know the steps
quiz.explain: Making drinks without a recipe shows the skills are truly learned.

quiz.q: Why teach a skill to someone else?
options: Teaching proves you really know it
quiz.explain: If you can teach it, you truly understand it.

days.title: Capstone Prep: Plan Your Final Drinks Night
days.goal: Plan your capstone drinks night and gather everything you need.
steps: Choose your capstone menu: three cocktails and two mocktails.
Write the full shopping list with costs.
Write the making order, starting with what takes longest.
Check you have every tool, glass, and ingredient.
Do a trial run of the hardest drink if you have time.
days.task: Write your complete capstone plan and cost it.
days.challenge: Do a trial run of your hardest capstone drink today.

options: Everything you learned: shaking, stirring, muddling, and costing
quiz.explain: The capstone proves the whole course.

quiz.q: Why start with what takes longest?
options: So everything finishes at the same time
quiz.explain: Long tasks start first so all drinks are ready together.

options: To find problems before the real night
quiz.explain: A trial run finds problems while there is still time to fix them.

capstone.title: The Drinks Night: Cocktails and Mocktails for Everyone
capstone.brief: Run a drinks night for your household or customers: serve three cocktails and two mocktails, each in the right glass, garnished neatly, and made to order. Cost every drink, serve responsibly, and collect feedback.
checks: Menu planned with recipes, costs, and prices
Three cocktails made well: shaken, stirred, and layered
Each drink in the right glass, garnished neatly
Drinks served cold and on time
Costs worked out and profit known
Feedback collected from at least one person who drank them
deliverables: A photo of your drinks menu and drinks
Your written menu with recipes, costs, and prices
Your making order, starting with what takes longest
Your signature cocktail recipe written in your own words
A short note on what you learned and what you will improve next
